title: Crawler Log Folder
description:
A file system maintains a log each time a user performs a change-folder operation starting from the main (root) folder:
- `"../"`: move to the parent folder of the current folder (if already in the main folder, remain in the main folder).
- `"./"`: remain in the same folder.
- `"x/"`: move to the child folder named `x` (guaranteed to exist).

Given a list of strings `logs` representing the sequence of operations performed by the user, return the minimum number of operations needed to return to the main folder after all log operations are complete.
constraints: logs[i] contains lowercase English letters, digits, '.', and '/'.
logs[i] follows the format described in the statement.
hints: Directory navigation follows LIFO order: entering a child folder pushes onto the path stack, and '../' pops if non-empty.
Since only the final depth is needed, you can either maintain an explicit stack or simply track its size without dropping below 0.

examples.explanation: Entering d1, d2, backing out to d1, entering d21, and staying leaves depth 2.
Entering d1, d2, staying, entering d3, entering d31 leaves depth 3.
All parent operations at root stay at depth 0, and moving into d1 then backing out returns to depth 0.
